bib.title: Tutorial Proposal: Retrieval-based Language Models and Applications
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the ACL, Volume 6: Tutorial Abstracts, pages 41-46

question: What should a 3-hour tutorial cover to give an overview of retrieval-based language models: their architectures, training and applications?
hypothesis: Retrieval-based LMs overcome the limits of purely parametric LMs (size, long-tail knowledge, staleness, hallucination, privacy leakage).
contributions: A taxonomy of retrieval-based LM architectures by datastore granularity and by how retrieved information is integrated
A survey of scalable learning algorithms (pipelined, in-batch approximation, asynchronous index update)
Coverage of downstream adaptation and extensions beyond English text

results.claim: Retrieval-based LMs are sorted by how retrieved information is integrated: concatenated with the input, fused in intermediate layers, or interpolated at the output distribution.
results.setup: Taxonomy in a tutorial proposal; no evaluation.

results.claim: Retrieval-based LMs are sorted by datastore unit: text chunk, token, or entity mention.

results.claim: Retrieval-based LMs can outperform LMs without retrieval by a large margin with far fewer parameters (attributed to Mallen et al. 2022; no figure given).

limits: A proposal with no experiments, tables or measured numbers; every benefit is cited to other work without figures.
Authors concede retrieval-based LMs can still output plausible but incorrect text and can leak private data from the corpus.
Dated: 2023 scope, predates most LLM-era RAG practice.

terms.definition: incorporate a non-parametric datastore (e.g., text chunks from an external corpus) with their parametric counterparts
